mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is a consistent trend observed across multiple monetary policy cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of observations where FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (25th percentile of historical levels).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment above 4.5% signals economic distress, triggering immediate market pessimism and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monetary easing (FEDFUNDS ≤ 4.0%) and labor market deterioration (UNRATE rising >0.2pp) signal dual economic stress, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 4.0% AND UNRATE increases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances despite FEDFUNDS ≤ 4.0% and UNRATE rise >0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, declining housing starts below 1600 thousand units signal weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of observations during late-cycle expansions with HOUST < 1600 thousand units.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days as a consistent trend.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of observations where HOUST shows a sustained upward trend (3-month increase >1.5%).

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting market expectations of tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 102.5) combined with weak GDP growth (GDPC1 < 1.0% annualized) signals supply-side contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances despite INDPRO < 102.5 and GDPC1 < 1.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recoveries, sustained payroll growth above 100 thousand per month signals labor market strength, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of observations during post-recession recoveries with PAYEMS > 100 thousand monthly growth.
